details.name: MOB.385_Work_Failure_Edit_Save
details.message:
`MOB.385` **A failure's `Edit Item` saves — proved on the server, then restored.**
- The fixture's permanent failure (`Pump 0102 · BELT (R-L1) · MISSED · TIME`): the form
  opens prefilled, Repair Type **MISSED → REPAIR** on the FIRST `Edit Item` after the page
  loads (`UPDATE_WORKSTAGE_FAILURE`), proved by a `/graphql` read of that failure id, then
  **REPAIR → MISSED** and proved again (`always`).
- REPAIR, not ADJUST: `MOB.391` owns the ADJUST key (bugs §40's unique key).
- 🛑 **Red whenever bugs §42's race is lost:** that first Submit does nothing (the form's schema is
  built before `GET_SCHEMA` loads). The save proof is soft, so the restore still runs.
- The restore opens and closes `Edit Item` once first, so it saves with §42 open or fixed.
- 🛑 SELF-RESTORING — one field, restored to a fixed value.

steps.name: Navigate to the fixture work order (premise)
Let the detail view begin rendering
Test work order detail rendered
Open the Failure tab
Let the failure cards render
PREMISE: exactly one `Pump 0102 · BELT (R-L1) · MISSED · TIME` card on screen
PREMISE (server): the fixture's one failure is BELT (R-L1) · MISSED · TIME — the fixed restore value
Remove the server read's sessionStorage keys

params.code:
['__dd385_server', '__dd385_server:inflight', '__dd385_server:at'].forEach(k => sessionStorage.removeItem(k));
return true;

steps.name: Open the `Pump 0102 · BELT (R-L1) · TIME` failure card's gear — exactly one such card reading MISSED
Let the menu open
Click `Edit Item`
Let the edit form mount (it loads the WorkStageFailure schema)
The failure form opened
The form opened PREFILLED from this card: `#failureTypeId` BELT (R-L1), `#repairTypeId` MISSED, `#rootCauseTypeId` TIME

params.code:
const v = id => { const el = document.getElementById(id); return el ? (el.value || '').trim() : null; };
return v('failureTypeId') === 'BELT (R-L1)' && v('repairTypeId') === 'MISSED' && v('rootCauseTypeId') === 'TIME';

steps.name: Focus the Repair Type lookup (`#repairTypeId`)
Wait for the repair type options
Pick REPAIR — the one VISIBLE option titled exactly "REPAIR"
The form now holds Repair Type REPAIR

params.code:
const el = document.getElementById('repairTypeId');
return !!el && (el.value || '').trim() === 'REPAIR';

steps.name: Failure Type and Root Cause are still BELT (R-L1) / TIME (no cascade cleared them)

params.code:

return v('failureTypeId') === 'BELT (R-L1)' && v('rootCauseTypeId') === 'TIME';

steps.name: Submit is ARMED — `button[form="work-failure-form"]` is `type="submit"` (trap 8)

params.code:
const b = document.querySelector('button[form="work-failure-form"]');
return !!b && b.type === 'submit';

steps.name: Submit the edit
Let the update reach the server
⭐ SERVER: the FIRST `Edit Item` after the page loads SAVED — the same failure now holds Repair Type REPAIR (bugs §42: red until fixed; the modal proves nothing here)
Remove the server read's sessionStorage keys

params.code:
['__dd385_server', '__dd385_server:inflight', '__dd385_server:at'].forEach(k => sessionStorage.removeItem(k));
return true;
